page.overview:
What is Cornelius Oswald Fudge?

Minister Cornelius Oswald Fudge, , was a British wizard who served as the thirty-second Minister for Magic of the British Ministry of Magic, in office from 1990 to 1996. Although reliant on the advice of Albus Dumbledore at first, by the height of his power, he had complete control of the Ministry of Magic, as well as extensive influence over the publishing of the Daily Prophet.

Fudge began his career in the Ministry as Junior Minister in the Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes. He was chosen to succeed Millicent Bagnold as Minister for Magic, He thus had the responsibility of meeting with the Muggle Prime Minister when necessary, which became increasingly frequent with the advent of the Second Wizarding War.

Fudge's tenure saw a marked increase in pure-blood supremacy both within the Ministry of Magic and throughout the larger British wizarding community, all directing towards the eventual Return of Lord Voldemort in 1995. When Ginevra Weasley was possessed by Tom Riddle's Diary to commit attacks on Muggle-born students at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, Fudge was involved in suspending Dumbledore and incarcerating Rubeus Hagrid, the suspected attacker. Later, he was forced to deal with the escape of the assumed Death Eater and mass-murderer Sirius Black, who was also innocent. Although Fudge and the Ministry came close to apprehending Black, Black ultimately escaped from Fudge's fingers.

Death Eater activity heightened after the 422nd Quidditch World Cup, hosted in Great Britain, where the celebrations were followed by a Death Eater terrorist attack and where the Dark Mark illuminated the skies for the first time in thirteen years. This activity only heightened during the subsequent Triwizard Tournament, but Fudge refused to believe Harry Potter's claim that Cedric Diggory's had been murdered at the hands of Lord Voldemort. Fudge leveraged the Daily Prophet to silence Potter,
